narrative.overview: The site reads as a clearing at golden hour. Amber is the light that falls through the canopy; cream parchment is the page it lands on; oxblood is the ink. Everything else is paper, bark, and leaf. The system is warm before it is modern, and hand-bound before it is systematic. There is one page material and two inks: light mode is a single sheet of pale cream paper warmed at its left and right edges, dark mode is the same room after sunset. Body copy is ink on paper in both modes; amber never becomes text colour, because amber here is light, and light does not carry meaning. The system runs two registers. The default register is the garden: calm, reading-first, one column, with craft concentrated in the ruled h2, the SVG page divider and the bark-plaque code block. The second register is the tabletop handbook, activated only under the D&D route classes.
keyCharacteristics: Amber primary with a seven-step ramp; oxblood heading ink in light mode, amber heading ink in dark mode.
Warm, low-opacity shadows tinted amber (never neutral grey) on paper surfaces.
Irregular compound corner radii for anything that reads as a cut sheet or a plaque.
Reading-first density: 16px body at 1.625 line height, 280px sidebar, one content column.
Craft artifacts over ornament: SVG divider, ruled h2, leaf-lit code plaque.
Handbook sub-theme that is explicitly scoped to a route and never leaks.

rules.name: The Two Inks Rule
rules.body: Amber is light; ink is text. Body copy is never amber and never a link colour. If a passage needs emphasis, it gets weight or oxblood, not the accent.

rules.name: The Gilded Edge Rule
rules.body: The warm gradient on body lives in the first and last 1% of the horizontal axis and nowhere else. A new surface does not get its own gradient; it sits flat on the sheet.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Amber is the only interactive hue. Oxblood, the leaf trio, and the ledger greys never become hover or focus colours.

rules.name: The 16/26 Rule
rules.body: Body copy is 16px on a 26px line (1.625). A 110% base was tried and replaced; do not reintroduce it.

rules.name: The Handbook Quarantine Rule
rules.body: BookInstanity, MrEavesRemake, ScalySans, the drop cap and the small-caps first line apply only inside html[class*="-doc-id-DnD/"]. They never appear on a dashboard, a landing page, or a general article.

rules.name: The Two-Weight Rule
rules.body: Reading text uses 400, emphasis 450 to 700, and mono never exceeds 450. Weight is the system's emphasis tool; colour is not.

rules.name: The Warm Shadow Rule
rules.body: If a shadow falls on paper, it is rgba(163, 106, 0, ...). Black shadows are an exception for the handbook container and dark-mode hovers, not a default.

rules.name: The Settle Rule
rules.body: Hover does not scale, bounce or glow. It changes the shadow from rest to lifted over 0.2s ease-in-out. Motion is a sheet being picked up, nothing faster.

dos: Do keep body copy at 16px on a 26px line (1.625), and keep paragraph margins tight (0.5em bottom).
Do give every h2 the full-width 2px gold rule, and give h3 nothing.
Do use the compound radius 28px 12px 35px 15px for anything that reads as a cut sheet: code blocks, admonitions, terminal frames.
Do tint paper shadows amber (rgba(163, 106, 0, .4) at rest, .7 on hover) and animate them over 0.2s ease-in-out.
Do reach for --ifm-color-primary and its seven-step family instead of writing new amber hex values.
Do use the SVG divider on hr, and the leaf trio on full-width terminal frames only.
Do scope handbook typography and the parchment texture to the -doc-id-DnD/ route classes, and give those components their own --dnd-* tokens.
Do prefer a 9999px pill or a 3px hairline to a mid-range radius; the system has no 12px-to-24px middle ground.
donts: Don't set body copy in amber, and don't make amber a heading colour in light mode. Headings are oxblood there.
Don't put the warm gradient anywhere except the first and last 1% of the viewport edges.
Don't introduce a fourth accent hue. Amber, oxblood and the decorative leaf trio are the whole palette.
Don't use neutral grey shadows on paper surfaces; the dark-mode card hover (#AAA3) and the handbook container are the only exceptions.
Don't reuse the handbook's red rule (#9c2b1b) as an error colour, or the leaf red as a danger state.
Don't ship new white-on-amber text. #fff on #e99700 sits near 2.1:1; the existing active pill does this and is a known exception, not a pattern to copy.
Don't apply the organic radius, the leaf trio or the drop cap outside their artifacts. They are signatures, and repeating them everywhere spends them.
Don't put a hardcoded type size in a component CSS module when an Infima variable already carries it.
